text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- Leading party the Democratic Party Saimnieks sent a letter to General Prosecutor Janis Skrastins asking him to check whether Saimnieks ministers in the government have violated the anti-corruption law.

- President Guntis Ulmanis met U.S. Ambassador Larry Napper who the U.S. will soon finalise a plan for Baltic security, called the Baltic Action plan. To sign the charter, President Bill Clinton may invite the Baltic presidents to Washington.
- Riga City Council raised rents and set a maximum of 14.8 centimes per square metre.
DIENA
- The cabinet accepted the basics of the 1998 state budget. The total increase of the budget is expected to be 9.9 percent.
- The leaders of the three biggest parliamentary factions cannot agree on amending the anti-corruption law.

- During a meeting of defence ministers of the Baltic and Nordic countries in Estonia, Norwegian Defence Minister Jorgen Cosmo said the Baltic countries will not be admitted to NATO in the first stage of expansion due to their weak defence system.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE

- Representatives of nationalist party For Fatherland & Freedom in Riga city council said the council should pull down the Red Army monument the Victory Monument after it was hit by a bomb blast. Other parties say it should be repaired.
- Economy Minister Guntars Krasts announced that all legal entities in Latvia can deal with privatisation vouchers without a special license.
- The leader of the Social Democratic Workers Party Arnis Mugurevics announced that his left-wing party will be a leading force in advancing Latvia towards the EU.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- A BMW owned by the general director of the Imperial Trade Company was blown up in Riga.
- The agreement merging oil pipeline operator LaSam with Ventspils Nafta will be concluded mid-July. The merger marks the start of the privatisation process of Ventspils.
- Finance Minister Roberts Zile wants to develop a unified system of supervision of financial institutions.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- Turkish company Mesa Housing Industries Incorporated plans to begin building a supermarket and entertaiment complex early in 1998, investing about $35-40 million. The work may take 16 to 18 months.
